This interaction is supported by two distinct pathways, both of which indicate that Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside acts as a target for Guanylate cyclase soluble subunit alpha-2 and subsequently for Citrusinol, which in turn targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The scores from these paths suggest a moderate level of confidence in the relationship, though the exact nature of the interaction remains partially inferred. The presence of multiple targets in the pathway implies that Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside may influence the activity of the transporter family member 1B1 through a series of intermediate molecules, potentially affecting anion transport in cellular processes. The integration of these pathways highlights the complexity of the relationship, emphasizing the need for further experimental validation to confirm the direct involvement of Taxifolin 3-O-beta-D-xylopyranoside in the regulation of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1.
